verdict.rationale: Convex documents per-user access control as authorization rules written in code inside its server functions, which run in the database and check every public request. It explicitly says it does not use an RLS-style framework, so there are no declarative row-level policies or security-rules language; you write the checks in each function. Missing for 10: declarative RLS policies or a security-rules system, detailed docs on per-user row filtering patterns, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can restrict data access per user with row-level security policies or security rules

citations.quote: This architecture lets you check every public request against any authorization rules you can define in code.
Convex doesn't need an opinionated authorization framework like RLS, which is required in client oriented databases like Firebase or Supabase.
This flexibility lets you build and use an authorization framework for your needs.
